Worked: r'(t)=<-sin t,cos t,1>, r'(0)=<0,1,1> at (1,0,0), speed sqrt2 constant; r(2t) same helix at 2sqrt2. Old Q3 explanation uses banned word "crucial" (out of scope, not changed).
Checked <2t,4t^2> gives y=x^2; <t^2,t^3> has r'(0)=0 and a cusp.
Triangle-equality condition (same direction or one zero) is correct.
Worked: integrands 1 and 0 on the unit circle; circulations 2pi and 0; potential 1/2(x^2+y^2) correct.

Checked <0,x^2>: circulation integral of cos^3 t over [0,2pi] = 0, curl 2x nonzero. Checked <-y,x>/(x^2+y^2) gives 2pi on the unit circle. Old Explainer uses banned word "crucial" (out of scope, not changed).

Said "nonzero curl anywhere inside a loop produces nonzero circulation around it"; false (curl can cancel; the new mis bullet's <0,x^2> is a counterexample). Replaced with: circulation around a counterclockwise simple loop equals the total curl over the enclosed region.
